answer: A per-action escrow makes each verified claim cost real money: an agent stakes a bond sized to the task, and the bond is slashed only after a quorum of cross-attestations confirms the work. Faking a thousand identities means floating a thousand bonds, so the attacker's outlay scales linearly with influence while honest agents recover stake on success. Like a beacon across a widening ocean, each paid action outlives its issuer, letting the network price trust at the horizon of real repeat cost rather than at free account creation.
